# Zenvim

> Zenvim is a lightweight Neovim configuration for Termux on Android. It starts in 40–70 ms, loads plugins lazily with lazy.nvim, and ships LSP, completion, Telescope and mini.files — tuned for low-end devices and on-screen keyboards. Free and open source under GPL-3.0.

- [Overview](https://nurmuhammedjoy.github.io/zenvim/): what Zenvim is and what it includes.
- [Features](https://nurmuhammedjoy.github.io/zenvim/#features): startup time, plugins, language servers.
- [Install](https://nurmuhammedjoy.github.io/zenvim/#install): one command in Termux, or a manual git clone.
- [Keymaps](https://nurmuhammedjoy.github.io/zenvim/#keymaps): full default keymap list; leader key is Space.
- [Plugins](https://nurmuhammedjoy.github.io/zenvim/#plugins): every bundled plugin by group.
- [Source](https://github.com/nurmuhammedjoy/zenvim): GitHub repository, issues and pull requests.

## Requirements

- Termux on Android (installed from F-Droid)
- Neovim 0.11.0 or newer (`pkg install nvim`)
- Git (`pkg install git`)

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nurmuhammedjoy/zenvim/main/build | bash
```

The installer backs up any existing `~/.config/nvim` to `~/.config/nvim.bak`. It only works inside Termux on Android.

## Facts

- Type: Neovim configuration (dotfiles), not a Neovim plugin.
- Platforms: Android via Termux. Not supported on desktop Linux, macOS or Windows.
- License: GNU GPL v3.0.
- Author: nurmuhammedjoy.
- Language servers: HTML, CSS, TypeScript, JSON, Emmet and Bash via Mason; `clangd` and `lua_ls` are picked up from `$PATH`.
